subject.title: docs(install): recommend Node 26 as the OpenClaw runtime

question: Should OpenClaw deliberately make non-LTS Node 26 the fresh-install default before it enters LTS in October 2026, while CI and release validation remain on Node 24?
rationale: This is a support and release-policy choice, not a mechanical installer correction: the PR intentionally changes the runtime users receive and the project recommendation despite an upstream Current-versus-LTS split.

options.title: Retain Node 24 for fresh installs
options.body: Restore the Node 24 installer and documentation default while preserving Node 26 as a supported opt-in runtime until it reaches LTS.

options.title: Adopt Node 26 before LTS
options.body: Explicitly accept the Current-line support risk, align every installer path including Windows, and require inspectable multi-platform runtime evidence before merge.

options.title: Pause until Node 26 LTS
options.body: Defer the default change until the upstream October 2026 LTS transition and revisit it with the release baseline.

recommendation.title: Retain Node 24 for fresh installs
recommendation.body: Restore the Node 24 installer and documentation default while preserving Node 26 as a supported opt-in runtime until it reaches LTS.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR’s author supplied the runtime benchmark rationale and implemented every proposed default change; confidence is limited because current-main history could not be inspected.
